column3: The Hebrew has dwelling places in the plural; BSB has dwelling place.
The Hebrew says bird rather than explicitly sparrow and does not explicitly add near before Your altars as BSB does.
The Hebrew names highways in their heart, without explicitly saying pilgrimage; it begins with a singular man, then uses their.
The Hebrew names a spring in the singular and blessings; BSB has a place of springs and pools.
The Hebrew has a singular verb for appearing without explicitly saying each or until, which BSB supplies.
The Hebrew says look at the face without explicitly adding with favor as BSB does.
The Hebrew does not explicitly add elsewhere to the thousand days and describes a completed choice of standing at the threshold.
